title: How Java recognizes marker interfaces
answer: A marker interface has no required methods; its presence on a class carries type metadata. Java can distinguish marked classes through normal type checks such as instanceof or Class.isAssignableFrom(...), and frameworks can inspect implemented-interface metadata through reflection. The JDK historically uses marker interfaces such as Serializable and Cloneable to signal special semantics.
